title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure. A synthetic video of a well-known financial sector personality was used as the front of an investment fraud, and the victim saw what appeared to be that person advertising an opportunity with promised significant returns. The false claim of identity did the work, not a false claim about a product.

The failure sat at first contact, in an advertisement the victim encountered before any verification of who was behind it. From there the fraud moved to WhatsApp, to pressure for further payments, to multiple online accounts opened by the victim, to remote access given to the fraudsters' computers under the guise of help, and to borrowed money sent to accounts controlled by criminals. Catching it at the point of contact would have required confirming that the person in the video had actually endorsed the investment and checking Financial Conduct Authority authorisation for whoever was being dealt with.

What is not established is who the personality was, since the PSNI did not name them, and no arrest, charge or verdict appears in the reporting. The similar scams using Martin Lewis, Peter Jones and Steven Bartlett are separate cases seen by BBC News NI, not findings about this one.

reports.title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

summary:
A person in the Ards and north Down area lost £250,000 after an AI-generated video scam. The Police Service of Northern Ireland said the victim saw what looked like a video of a well-known financial sector personality. It advertised an investment opportunity and promised significant returns. The PSNI did not name the celebrity. BBC News NI has seen similar scams using financial experts such as Martin Lewis, Peter Jones and Steven Bartlett.

After a small initial investment, the victim was contacted on WhatsApp and urged to pay more. The fraudsters persuaded them to open multiple online accounts and gave remote access to their computer, saying they were helping. Police called it a sophisticated and substantial fraud. The victim was encouraged to borrow money, and funds went to accounts controlled by criminals. Superintendent Joanne Gibson urged people to stop and check financial activity and for families to discuss fraud. Police advised verifying who they deal with and checking Financial Conduct Authority authorisation.
title_en: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity
